parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files all handle one concern: they declare the domain-layer repository ports for the aggregate entities (Project, Task, User). Each interface follows the same pattern. findById returns Entity | null, and save(entity) returns void. Each one depends only on its own domain entity. TaskRepository adds query methods scoped to a project (findByProjectId, findByProjectIdAndStatus, findByProjectIdAndAssignee). These are lookups specific to that aggregate, not a separate concern. No business rule or invariant is stated in more than one place, because the files only declare method signatures. No file goes around the module's abstractions. Repeating findById/save in each interface is the normal repository-port style, not a duplicated invariant. A shared generic base interface could remove that repetition, but leaving it out doesn't break the rubric. The graph supports this reading: use cases inject these interfaces through their constructors, and the in-memory infrastructure classes implement them one-to-one.
